messages.subject: Output piared data set naming
messages.body_plain:
I am using MatchIT through an SPSS shell called* Propensity Score Matching
for SPSS version 3.0.4 by Felix Thoemmes*.  I like the SPSS shell because
it provides a seamless process for me.

I have two questions:
First, I am matching schools in two states and need to run the matching
twice once for each state.  I am wondering if there is a way to run matchit
with a strata for states so that I can get balance statistics for each
state separately as well as balance with all school combined across states.

Second, The output provides the paired data set and names it with a random
number.  This makes it difficult to save the paired data using syntax (it
is named differently on  each run).  I understand that the random number
reduces the likelihood that files will be over written however, I am
wondering if it is possible to set the random seed so that the file name
remains constant across runs.

Thanks
Bill



--

Professor - Public Health Education
The School of Health and Human Sciences
The University of North Carolina at Greensboro

messages.subject: Re: Output piared data set naming
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bill,
On your two questions:

1.  No, unfortunately there isn’t an easy way to automatically get that kind of stratified balance statistics and overall balance statistics from MatchIt.  You would just have to run the matching twice and then obtain the combined summary statistics yourself.

2.  I think that random number issue is specific to the SPSS shell; you may want to reach out to Felix to see if there is a way to change that.  (When using matchit in R that isn’t how the paired dataset is output).

Thanks,
Liz

messages.subject: ATE for Full Matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to calculate the ATE weights after conducting full matching.
There was a reference to the following documentation for the calculation of
ATT weights, but the access was denied:
https://lists.gking.harvard.edu/pipermail/matchit/2011-September/000312.html

Given the following notation:
n = overall sample size,
n*i *= sample size within stratum *i*,
n*t* = no. of treatment subjects in overall sample,
n*c* = no. of comparison subjects in overall sample,
n*ti* = no. of treatment subjects within stratum *i*, and
n*ci* = no. of comparison subjects within stratum *i*,

Is the ATE weights for the treatment and subject in stratum *i*
 respectively:

ATEweight*ti* = ( n*i* / n*ti* ) * ( n*t* / n )

ATEweight*ci* = ( n*i* / n*ci* ) * ( n*c* / n ) ?

By extension, would this also be the way to calculate the ATE weights after
subclassification?

Many thanks,
Yi Xe

messages.subject_clean: Data warning message for full matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I ran a command for full matching, but keep getting a warning message. Is
there something missing in the way I wrote the command, or do I need to set
up the data in a special way for full matching?

Also, what are the implications of ignoring the warning?

*Command:*
    m.out <- matchit (treat ~ X1 + X2 + X3
                    + X4 + X5 + ...+Xn ,
                    data = df4w1, method = "full", distance = "logit")
    summary(m.out, standardize = TRUE)

*Warning message:*
In fullmatch(d, ...) :
  Without 'data' argument the order of the match is not guaranteed to be
the same as your original data.

Many thanks,
Yi Xe

messages.subject: Re: ATE for Full Matching
messages.body_plain:
IPTW will give you an estimate within strata.  You then compute the
weighted average of those strata-specific ATE estimates where the weights
are proportional to the strata size.

Kosuke Imai
Professor, Department of Politics
Center for Statistics and Machine Learning
Princeton University
http://imai.princeton.edu
